item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I love the feel of this. The bookends, with the unnamed character running to civilization on the horizon as the sun begins to rise. How he got there, from curious L2 amidst vague rumors all the way up to renegade O5 (that was a bit unclear — was he promoted, or was he there for some other reason?)…from scraping the surface to finding himself deeper than he ever imagined. I can't think of a way to describe the atmosphere of this piece, but I really, really like it.

I'm not sure how I feel about the portrayal of the O5s, regularly going around and interacting freely with lower levels, to the point where people can recognize them on sight (I can see L4s personally meeting with O5s, but even then I expect they'd only know the faces of their own superiors). It works well for a loose side branch of my mental multiverse, but in my primary headcanon, I feel like it would be seen as far too much of a security and safety risk for the most important personnel in the Foundation to attend parties and visit construction sites. Of course, individual headcanon is the order around here, so that's not really a problem with the tale, just my own feelings.

But above all, I just really want to draw attention to this one line (which is the preview line in the featured tale archive, so it already has the emphasis it deserves, but still):

Who are they? Oh, they have numbers, not names. Who were they? Fuck knows.

This. This is exactly it. I've always found myself fascinated with the O5s, and this line just says it all so perfectly. I want to grab it and never let it go. Who were these enigmatic figures all the way at the top? They don't have names anymore. Just…numbers. In a twisted way, I'd even venture to say they're no more human than D-Class. Sure, there are a thousand differences between the two — power, intelligence, morality…but they're both alone, one up at the top, one down at the bottom, with nobody but their own to think of them as people.

item.content:encoded:
Like. Seven *knows* about 001? Meaning he knows the Foundation only exists to contain him? And yet he chooses to remain contained… except for when he's jetsetting via heicopter or dominating world governments?

*she

*her

*she

*she's

:P seriously now.

And there's a lot that's unsaid in the story. You're kinda doing the thing where you assume that an unreliable narrator is unreliable in every single way, and that the Foundation is all-powerful. And that just because the O5s (or Seven, at least) knows that the Council is 001 or the equivalent, that means that they (or she) knows it's 'containing' them (and/or isn't fine with it). And you're also assuming that the jetsetting and dominating world governments isn't part of the containment — in fact, the story makes it very clear that it is. There's no reason to assume the other things either, though.

Plus, there's no way that the conspiracy plan overall is the memetic effect talking, although I can buy the briefcase having a memetic effect that plays into such conspiracy plans, since perhaps only someone who's already thinking CONSPIRACY would be exposes to that memetic effect. Memes are cultural ideas, after all, and conspiracy theories are a prime example of memes, as is paranoia about government organizations and such. Maybe the briefcase has an interpretation effect that is designed to slot right in to someone's conspiratorial ideas if they already have them already.

Minus those issues, though, I don't see why the rest wouldn't be a feasible interpretation (though not the only one, although, hey, if you got it spot-on, then I'm sure Light will eventually verify!). Perhaps the narrator is wrong and this is part of the plan all along. =)

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
So, wait…

+ Show
- Hide

The Foundation was built to contain the 05 council, but the 05 council knows what's in the briefcase, which is allegedly all the secrets of the Foundation, presumably up to and including the nature of SCP-001, which the protagonist surmises is the fact that the SCP foundation was built to contain the council?

Bullshit. That narrative doesn't even make sense from the protagonist's point of view. Let alone the rest of the characters. Like. Seven *knows* about 001? Meaning he knows the Foundation only exists to contain him? And yet he chooses to remain contained… except for when he's jetsetting via heicopter or dominating world governments? And why would the Foundation then make more O5s by promoting people from within?

The whole story is a snake eating its own tail. Or at least, it would be, if anything the protagonist thought were true was what was actually going on here. But if we start with the assumption that the protagonist is full of crap, the rest quickly becomes clear:

This was all an elaborate prank.

The Briefcase is pretty obviously an SCP-Object that makes you think it contains incriminating documents. The 05 Council knowingly exposed him to it, either as one final test of his loyalty or else as a practical joke. It probably has been feeding his paranoia and curiosity, compelling him to grab it and run, ever since he first laid eyes on it.

That's why his conspiracy theory is so vague and self-contradictory— it's mostly the memetic effect talking!

Perhaps someone more loyal wouldn't have taken the bait, or perhaps this is the traditional hazing before someone becomes a full O5. Either way, it's pretty clear to me that the contents of the briefcase are irrelevant. As is most of the actual flight from the Foundation.

The extent to which he's been successful at making off with the briefcase has nothing to do with lax security, his skill at dodging sniper bullets, or his brilliant escape plan. It has everything to do with the fact that the entire O5 council is watching him via satellite feed and laughing into their drinks as he makes that final mad dash towards the Embassy.

- Hide

Great story. Sorry for firing my headcannon at it. But. Come on, I can't be the only one who sees this, right? :D

Edit: looks like Abettik had a similar thought, but took it in a different direction. Actually, Abettik's interpretation ties in the Chaos Insurgency angle so neatly that I'm starting to suspect I'm wrong and he's right. Chekov's Gun and all that. This story made such great use of foreshadowing with Brenda's cell that it's easy to imagine other scenes serving a dual purpose.

item.content:encoded:
+1

Hmmm… I came up with a COMPLETELY different observation than anyone else. In my mind, this story is about someone experiencing…

+ Show
- Hide

…a subliminal memetic effect without realizing it.

The Chaos Insurgency cooked up some subconscious memetic suggestion that it could innocuously spread through the Foundation ranks, getting people to subconsciously betray the Foundation under the guise of "Freedom of Information" and "the Foundation is Evil" and all that hippy stuff. Except this one, the "Flytrap," was specifically designed to only work on people who attained a high enough security clearance… after all, I'm sure the Chaos Insurgency already knows most of the boring level 3 stuff.

Howey was either infected or an outright Chaos agent which is why he was taken away. Either way, he spread it to our narrator during a drunken night and the Foundation didn't know. The O5s had a suspicion. Or at least a failsafe. So when this guy finally got up to Level 4 or whatever, they presented him with an opportunity too good to pass up. It was CLEARLY a test.

Now let me emphasize: whatever this story is, there is NO WAY the briefcase contains anything important in it.

First of all, no one would believe ANYTHING about the Foundation written down anywhere without real proof. Seriously, try running into a CIA base with a briefcase full of printed out skips and see where it gets you.

Second of all, it was too clearly laid out, such an obvious trap. "Here's our one briefcase with all our secrets! Don't take it! Wink wink!" Yeah right.

Thirdly, the Foundation has the ability to Contain just about anything. They've got entire cities under quarantine, entire sections of ocean guarded by military fleets. One guy with a briefcase? There's no way he's bringing it down with a briefcase of _anything_. The briefcase could contain a group of sapient, talking apples all screaming Foundation secrets. They would contain it easily. No way this is happening. Simply not possible.

Fourthly, the narrator who's spent the last 10+ years in the Foundation should damn well know all of this. The. only. possible. motivation for him to somehow conveniently forget ALL of this, and think that he can run twenty goddamn miles without so much as a guard on a moped following him is plot-induced-stupidity. Or in this case, memetic-induced stupidity. His memetic Chaos virus makes him conveniently forget that the Foundation is capable of literally erasing him and his entire family from existence within five minutes of learning of his "escape."

Ten seconds after part 1, a helicopter with MTFs appears, they tranquilize him, and put him in a memetic containment cell.

- Hide
